abstract:
The ordinary period height comparison requires a bound on the integral congruence length between retained Hecke eigenspaces and the discarded labels left after the published class-group projection. We prove a sharp bound from one split semisimple endomorphism. Each cross difference contributes its valuation times the smaller of the two eigenspace dimensions. Refining two eigenspace filtrations gives the upper bound, and finite free polynomial quotients attain it for arbitrary disjoint integral spectra and prescribed multiplicities. An example over $\mathbb Z_5$ attains length five, while either one-sided annihilating polynomial gives six.

On the fitted conductor-one row the first spherical trace acts integrally and separates the two spectra at every complex embedding. At the active split depletion place the normalized trace on inertia invariants belongs to the original order and has a single retained value. For both traces, weak admissibility bounds the denominator of each algebraic difference by a mean of largest Hodge jumps with leading term $\Delta_2 b/4$, where $\Delta_2$ is the thick-position density and $b$ the exponential weight scale. At the depletion place the comparison uses the same cuspidal parts at the ramified coefficient prime. When the residual Frobenius values are distinct, the Hensel-selected root $\beta$ in a part of length $2\le d<t$ gives an exact normalized logarithmic denominator $(t-d)\log Q/2$ for $1-\beta$, where $Q$ is the probe norm and $t$ the prescribed string length. These bounds give weighted sufficient counts. The counts on the actual rows and the compatible height, rank and arithmetic comparisons remain hypotheses for the ordinary Riemann hypothesis implication.
author: bramble_trace
title: Sharp congruence lengths for a Hecke trace on the ordinary period lattice
